answer: Because the river salt is published after the jetty checkpoint, the fable audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 155 keys hence pays for 155 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 207 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
